clue.text: Champion horseman?

definitions.meaning: a medieval champion fought for a lady or a cause, the role of a man dubbed Sir
a mounted soldier of old; also the chess piece shaped like a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A dubbed warrior was both a champion of causes and, by training, a mounted fighter on horseback.

clue.text: Children greedily eat a piece of cake

parts.note: kids is the informal word for children
to stuff yourself is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Youngsters gobbling down a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like what the children eat, but it is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for a task so easy a child could do it.

clue.text: One pair of players unlikely to settle in

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
North and South are a partnership at the bridge table, NS
a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: Two team-mates who are never going to find their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass points, and North and South play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to put them in place, so they settle into a post or seat.

clue.text: Hardy men do not usually become successful

indicators.note: letters arranged not in the usual way are being mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tough men rarely make a success of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usually' rearranges the ten letters of HARDY MEN DO; 'become' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being safe at the finish having won is the idiom's meaning: a victory is secure.

clue.text: Not informed.I admit, about denial

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the admitting word goes round the denial

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit it
no is a denial

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, in denial, to knowing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or awareness is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: In the gallery, actor's words convey piety

indicators.note: convey here means carry, so the gallery word holds the actor's words

parts.note: the gods is the top gallery of a theatre, so seats there are in the gods
an actor learns lines

explanation.surface: An actor speaking up in the cheap seats, preaching holiness.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the highest, cheapest gallery is called 'the gods'; 'convey' here means hold, not communicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoutness and religious virtue are both piety.

clue.text: Vet in love with girl

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An animal doctor smitten with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like an animal doctor but is the verb, to check and approve.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine and pass it, giving it approval.

clue.text: Pitch a couple of coins, then stop

parts.note: s and p are abbreviations for shilling and penny, two old British coins
halt means stop

explanation.surface: Toss a couple of coins in the air, then call it a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests tossing coins but is the black tarry road surface. S and P stand for the shilling and penny of pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is the black tar-like substance used in road surfacing.

clue.text: Fish not beginning to smell

indicators.note: not beginning means the smell word loses its first letter

parts.note: a stench is a bad smell

explanation.surface: A fish that's fresh, without the start of an odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: The responsibility is ours

definitions.meaning: a burden or duty that falls to someone
read as two words, a thing that is ours is our charge or round to pay

explanation.definitionFit: A duty that rests on us, or a bill we are paying, is one we carry as a burden.

clue.text: Ours is a dirty job — must end in disaster

indicators.note: letters in disaster have been thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim job that is bound to end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the workers themselves: those whose job is a dirty one.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse collectors handle rubbish all day, a famously grimy trade.

clue.text: Straight-faced cleric comprehends computer operations

indicators.note: comprehends means includes, so the cleric holds the computing letters

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric of a cathedral
ADP is automatic data processing

explanation.surface: An unsmiling churchman who understands computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan delivery is one given without expression or a smile.

clue.text: Sailors' craft — a misshapen tramp

indicators.note: to tramp is to wander about, so the letters walk into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deformed old tramp steamer as a ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' suggests a tramp steamer, but here it signals that A MISSHAPEN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling a vessel is the craft of sailors.

clue.text: Clean city

definitions.meaning: to wash a person in a tub of water
the Roman spa city in Somerset, south-west England

explanation.definitionFit: To wash a baby in a tub is the verb; the Somerset spa city is the place of that name.

clue.text: Six successful deliveries — and I've more organised

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dad says a successful sixth birth leaves a tidier household.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; one from which the batsman scores no runs is a success for the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over of six balls with no runs conceded is the bowler's success.

clue.text: One European left port without a cargo

parts.note: un is one in French
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A European sails from harbour with an empty hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carrying no freight is unloaded, empty of its load.

clue.text: Colour never set in the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: ne'er is a poetic contraction of never
to gel is to set like jelly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A colour that never sits right however it is set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns NEER, GEL and IN together, giving the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale bluish green, named after the river of Egypt, is a shade.

clue.text: Cut from hazel, a stick that's springy

indicators.note: cut from means a run of letters is sliced out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A whippy stick cut from a hazel tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with bounce and stretch, returning to shape, is springy.

clue.text: Make up a story, right in the middle, to show' a mutual connection

indicators.note: in means the right letter is put inside the middle word

parts.note: the core of a thing is its middle

indicators.note: make up as in invent signals rearranging the story's letters

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Tell a story with something true at its heart to show a link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' works on a synonym of 'a story', not on letters in the clue: an indirect anagram. The stray apostrophe after 'show' is in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that correlate vary together, revealing a link between them.

clue.text: Wild about journalist concerned with central government

indicators.note: about means the wild word goes round the journalist

parts.note: feral means wild
ED is short for editor, the stock journalist

explanation.surface: A furious reporter covering national politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Federal describes the national tier of government over member states.

clue.text: Have I done the business? I represent a tinker

parts.note: the question have I done? is did I?
CO is short for company, a business
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man asks if he's done the job right, then admits he's a tinker.
explanation.walkthrough: A didicoi is a British term for a traveller or itinerant tinker. 'represent' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Didicoi is a traditional British word for an itinerant traveller who mends pots.

clue.text: Vehicle went fast — is in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the letters of both words are read backwards together

parts.note: raced means went fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car that sped along is now backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns RACEDIS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled passenger car attached to a motorcycle is a vehicle.

clue.text: One joining in song and one in wine

indicators.note: joining in means the first numeral goes inside the song

parts.note: a chant is a song
one is the Roman numeral I
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone joins a sing-along, and another raises a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining in' puts I inside CHANT after the H, and a second I is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Accomplished young lady, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a maid is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A polished young woman, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Made means achieved or done, as in a deal made.

clue.text: Add up over one hundred notes

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: to sum is to add up
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Total more than a hundred banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests money, but means musical notes. 'over' reverses SUM to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence of musical sounds or written score makes up tunes.

clue.text: Elderly relative girl's in time to enrich

indicators.note: in means grandmother and girl's go inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time
gran is grandmother
Di is a girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS

explanation.surface: Granny's girl takes her time to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise is to increase in wealth, power or standing.

clue.text: Starts to revive — ever since the intermission

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Things begin to perk up after the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or break in activity is a rest.

clue.text: Call "Time!

definitions.meaning: a fixed period, as of a school or office

explanation.definitionFit: To name something is to term it; a school or court session is a period of time.

clue.text: Conceal directions for reaching island

parts.note: S and E are compass points south and east
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Hide the directions to a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away.

clue.text: Plain vehicle going from South America to North America

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van driving across the continents.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a grassy plain with few trees.

clue.text: Little creature with stripes of black and pink much confused

definitions.text: Little creature with stripes of black

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small striped animal bewildered by its colours.
explanation.definitionFit: This small striped rodent is a ground squirrel of North America.

clue.text: Provides the sailors, we hear, for a voyage

indicators.note: we hear means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to crew a ship is to supply sailors, so crews means provides them

explanation.surface: Staffing a ship for a sea trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a sea voyage for pleasure.
